_meta.scope: PhysFormer-NI architecture feasibility on semi-synthetic NextGen VPP data

data_profile.scale: 5 households per portfolio, 6 portfolios (4 train / 1 val / 1 test)
data_profile.key_observation: The VPP is EXTREMELY small — aggregate load of 5 households is only ~5.5 kW. The net injection std is 6.2 kW. RMSE of 2.7 kW means the model's error is 44% of the signal std.

issues.title: 物理层 MAE=141 kW 说明 learnable physics parameters 近乎失效
issues.description: The physics layer achieves Theory MAE = 0.141 MW = 141 kW on portfolios whose aggregate load is only ~5.5 kW. This is 25× worse than the signal itself. The shared physics parameters (load_base, pv_scale, wind_scale, eta_charge_raw, etc.) are being optimized across ALL 6 portfolios simultaneously, but the portfolios have very different characteristics (load_heavy vs der_heavy vs mixed vs flex_heavy). The physics layer cannot capture cross-portfolio heterogeneity with shared scalar parameters.
issues.impact: The 'physics prior' is essentially a constant bias term. The data-driven residual is doing 98% of the predictive work. The architecture claim of 'physics-guided' is misleading — it's more accurately 'physics-initialized then almost entirely overridden by data.'
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) add per-portfolio physics parameters (portfolio-specific load_base, pv_scale, etc.), or (b) make the physics layer portfolio-aware by conditioning on portfolio embedding, or (c) accept that at this tiny scale the 'physics' is mostly a structural prior on functional form, not a useful quantitative estimate.

issues.title: 46% normalized error on a near-zero-mean signal — hard to claim 'good performance'
issues.description: The test set achieves RMSE/σ = 2.7/6.2 = 0.44 and MAE/σ = 2.0/6.2 = 0.32. For a VPP scheduling application, a normalized RMSE of 0.44 means the prediction error is nearly half the typical variation. A naive persistence forecast might achieve comparable or better results on such a small-scale, weather-driven signal. Without a persistence or climatology baseline, we cannot claim the model 'works well.'
issues.impact: The absolute numbers (2.7 kW RMSE, 2.0 kW MAE) sound impressive in isolation, but relative to the signal magnitude they are modest. The paper's claim of 'MSE-competitive with black-box baselines' cannot be evaluated without running Informer/iTransformer baselines on this exact dataset.
issues.suggested_fix: Run baseline models (Informer, iTransformer, simple LSTM, persistence, climatology) on the exact same train/val/test split. Report all metrics in both absolute (kW) and normalized (CV-RMSE, skill score) forms.

issues.title: Val MSE oscillation of ±30% in convergence plateau suggests overfitting to specific portfolios
issues.description: After epoch 23 (Val MSE=0.397), the Val MSE oscillates between 0.40 and 0.47 — a ±17% swing. With only 1 validation portfolio of 5 households, the validation set is too small to provide stable gradient signals. The model may be overfitting to the 4 training portfolios' specific load/solar patterns.
issues.impact: The reported 'best' Val MSE of 0.397 may be cherry-picked by epoch. A fair evaluation would average over the last N epochs or use an ensemble. More critically, with only 5 households per portfolio and 6 portfolios total, the benchmark may not generalize to the claimed domain of 'VPP forecasting.'
issues.suggested_fix: Report test-set metrics from a checkpoint selected by validation-set criteria (already done — epoch 24 is best val). Also report mean ± std over last 10 epochs to show stability. Consider increasing portfolio_size or number of portfolios for a more robust benchmark.

issues.title: Battery physics is the only genuine physics — but SOC dynamics are barely utilized
issues.description: The battery branch produces SOC trajectories that satisfy physical constraints (0% violations, 0% chg/dis overlap). However, the battery contributes negligibly to the net injection signal: p_battery_mw std is 3.3 kW, and the battery power oscillates around zero. The SOC consistency loss weight (0.1) is 10× smaller than net_mse, so the battery physics acts as a very weak regularizer. The 0% violation rates are achieved more by the signed-power parameterization (tanh guarantees |P|≤P_max and chg×dis=0) than by the loss.
issues.impact: The battery physics 'works' but doesn't matter much for the prediction. Removing the battery physics loss entirely (no_battery_physics_loss ablation) likely has minimal impact on net MSE. This weakens the claim that physics constraints improve prediction accuracy.
issues.suggested_fix: Run the no_battery_physics_loss ablation to quantify the battery physics contribution. If ΔMSE < 1%, the battery physics is structurally clean but not practically important for this dataset.

issues.title: Semi-synthetic wind is a systematic weakness — 15% penetration on a 5.5 kW portfolio = 0.8 kW mean wind
issues.description: The synthetic wind is generated from: (1) Rye microgrid wind template (Norway, not Australia), (2) ACT Canberra ERA5 wind speeds, (3) scaled to 15% annual energy penetration. The resulting wind signal has mean 0.8 kW and max 7.5 kW — a very narrow range. This limits the wind prediction challenge to essentially 'predict the wind speed → CF mapping.' The ERA5 wind speed has range [0.01, 10.8] m/s, which only covers the rising portion of the power curve (cut-in at ~1 m/s, rated at ~3 m/s, cut-out at ~5 m/s).
issues.impact: The 'wind forecasting' component of VPP prediction is trivialized by the narrow operating range. In a real VPP with MW-scale wind farms, the wind prediction challenge would be much harder. The dataset's wind synthesis limits the generality of any wind-related claims.
issues.suggested_fix: Document this limitation explicitly. Consider a sensitivity analysis varying wind penetration from 5% to 50% to show how model performance degrades with more challenging wind regimes.

issues.title: TemporalDecoder adds complexity but its benefit over FlattenHead is unquantified
issues.description: The TemporalDecoder (learnable query positions + cross-attention) replaces the simpler FlattenHead (Linear projection). But the no_temporal_decoder ablation wasn't run. Without this ablation, we don't know if the richer temporal decoder actually improves performance or just adds parameters.
issues.impact: A key architectural claim ('cross-attention temporal decoder is superior to linear projection') is untested. This could be a major ablation for the paper.
issues.suggested_fix: Run the FlattenHead ablation. If the performance difference is small, consider simplifying the architecture further.

issues.title: Single-climate, 5-household, 1-year benchmark may not generalize
issues.description: The dataset uses a single weather station (Canberra ACT), a single year (2018), and 5-household portfolios. A real VPP would span multiple climate zones, multiple years, and aggregate hundreds or thousands of assets. The current benchmark tests composition generalization (different households in train/val/test) but NOT climate generalization, temporal generalization, or scale generalization.
issues.impact: The methodology validation is limited in scope. The paper should clearly state these boundaries rather than implying general VPP applicability.
issues.suggested_fix: Document as limitations. The time-generalization benchmark (already built in the dataset) should be run as a secondary evaluation.

overall_assessment.summary: The PhysFormer-NI architecture is sound in design and achieves its primary goal (physically-consistent net injection prediction with competitive MSE). However, the extremely small VPP scale (5 households, 5.5 kW) and near-zero-mean target signal make the absolute performance numbers (2.7 kW RMSE) look better than they are in relative terms (44% normalized RMSE). The physics layer contributes primarily as a structural prior (functional form) rather than as a quantitative predictor (141 kW theory error). The architecture's main value proposition — 'physics guidance improves prediction' — is supported by the residual improvement (70× over theory alone) but this is largely because the theory is very weak rather than because the physics is very good.
key_strengths: Clean residual architecture with clear ablation paths
key_weaknesses: Physics layer contributes ~2% of predictive accuracy (98% from data-driven residual)
Test RMSE is 44% of signal std — modest for operational use
1 validation portfolio makes early stopping unreliable
Synthetic wind limits wind forecasting generality
No baseline comparisons run yet (Informer, iTransformer, persistence)
minimum_actions_before_publication: 1. Run Informer, iTransformer, and persistence baselines on same split
3. Report normalized metrics (CV-RMSE, skill score vs persistence)
4. Document portfolio heterogeneity as a limitation
5. Report epoch-stability metrics (mean ± std over last 10 epochs)
